translations.cfg_alert_0: Synchronous + No support: real-time sessions are difficult to manage without the trainer present to facilitate and moderate.

translations.cfg_alert_2: Production + No support: learners who must produce their own resources often need guidance and feedback.
translations.cfg_alert_3: Synchronous + Production + Collaborative + No support: very demanding configuration that requires a high level of autonomy and skills from learners.
translations.cfg_alert_4: Synchronous + Production + Collaborative (with support): this combination requires significant real-time coordination.
translations.cfg_alert_5: Large group + Strong support: individualized support becomes difficult with a large number of participants.
translations.cfg_alert_6: Distance + Synchronous: synchronous distance sessions require reliable tools and a good connection.
translations.cfg_alert_7: Distance + Large group + No support: learners can easily feel isolated and lost.
translations.cfg_alert_8: Distance + Collaborative: distance collaboration requires specific tools and rigorous organization.
translations.cfg_alert_9: Large group + Collaborative: organizing collaborative work with a large number of participants requires strong structuring.
translations.cfg_alert_10: Large group + Production: supporting resource production by a large group is demanding.
translations.cfg_alert_11: In-person + Asynchronous: this combination is inconsistent. If learners are present, prioritize synchronous interactions.

translations.persona_help_body:
1. What is a persona?
A persona is a fictional but realistic profile representing a segment of your target audience. It synthesizes data from observations, interviews or analyses to guide the design of adapted training programs.

2. How many personas to create?
Generally, 3 to 5 personas are enough to cover your audience's diversity. A single persona risks over-generalizing; beyond 7, complexity becomes hard to manage.

3. The 6 essential sections

  • Identity & Image: Name, avatar and key quote.
  • Demographics: Age, gender, education, position.
  • Work Context: Environment, time, constraints.
  • Preferences: Attitude, digital comfort, formats.
  • Gaps & Motivation: Level, barriers, benefits.
  • Learning Moments: When and how.

4. Usage
Fill in each section per persona, navigate between tabs, then export as JSON or Markdown.

translations.teacher_help_body:
1. Purpose
This canvas is used to describe a typical profile (persona) in order to design training programs that are truly adapted to needs, motivations, constraints and work contexts.

2. Toggle views (top of page)
Two switches control the display:

  • Basic / Advanced: enables advanced options to specify particular contexts (geography, infrastructure, specific challenges, etc.).
  • Suggestions: shows (or hides) the checkbox lists in all sections.

3. Fill in the persona

  • Free text: describe qualitative elements.
  • Suggestions: enable the toggle to display options, then check what applies.

4. Import & Export
The IMPORT & EXPORT section groups sharing and saving actions.

Note
This tool is an unofficial prototype.

translations.analysis_help_body:
1. What is a needs analysis?
A needs analysis is the first step in any instructional design process. It determines whether training is the appropriate response to a performance problem and, if so, defines its content and format.

2. The 8 sections

  • Clarification: understand and reformulate the initial request.
  • Organizational need: link the request to a measurable objective.
  • Desired performance: describe what learners should be able to do.
  • Current performance: document the current state and gap.
  • Task analysis: break down the work into concrete tasks.
  • Learner profile: understand the target audience.
  • Influencing factors: identify barriers and enablers.
  • Constraints: frame the project (budget, timeline, format).

3. Reference
Carliner, S. (2015). Training Design Basics (2nd ed.). ATD Press.

  • Influencing factors: identify barriers and enablers.
  • Constraints: frame the project (budget, timeline, format).

translations.analysis_gap_desc: Quantify the gap between current and optimal performance.
translations.analysis_ph_optimal: Describe the high standard of achievement expected. What should happen when the task is done perfectly?
translations.analysis_ph_actual: Describe what is currently happening. What are performers doing (or failing to do) that causes the problem?
translations.analysis_ph_gap_statement: E.g.: Actual: 10 units/h; Desired: 50 units/h; Gap: 40 units
translations.analysis_gap_statement_hint: This statement will be reused in the Evaluation phase.
translations.analysis_ph_frequency: How often does this error occur? Who is affected?
translations.analysis_filter_desc: Determine if instructional design is the appropriate solution.
translations.analysis_survival_question: Under ideal conditions and maximum motivation, would the people concerned be capable of performing the task correctly?
translations.analysis_survival_yes_hint: The cause is likely environmental or motivational. Training alone will not solve the problem.
translations.analysis_survival_no: NO – They would not be capable
translations.analysis_survival_no_hint: This is a knowledge or skill deficiency. An instructional intervention is appropriate.
translations.analysis_alert_non_instructional_text: The survival test suggests this problem stems from environmental or motivational factors. Consider management interventions, process changes, or job aids rather than a full training course.
translations.analysis_ph_tools: Do they have the necessary hardware, software, or workspace to perform?
translations.analysis_ph_procedures: Are the written instructions clear, up-to-date, and free of conflicting steps?
translations.analysis_ph_feedback: Do performers receive regular, timely information about the quality of their work?
translations.analysis_ph_consequences: Is correct performance being 'punished' (e.g., more work) or is non-performance being 'rewarded'?
translations.analysis_ph_value: Do learners understand why this task is important to the organization?
translations.analysis_ph_prerequisite: Did they ever know how to do it, or is this a completely new skill set?
translations.analysis_ph_complexity: Is the task performed so rarely that a job aid (checklist) would be more effective than a formal course?
translations.analysis_impact_desc: Build the business case for the intervention.
translations.analysis_ph_cost_inaction: What is this gap costing the organization in terms of money, time, safety, or reputation?
translations.analysis_ph_smart: Transform this gap into a Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Relevant, and Time-bound business target.
translations.analysis_smart_hint: This goal will be reused in the Evaluation phase (Level 4 - Results).
translations.media_subtitle: Evaluate the technical environment and select appropriate media
translations.media_section_1_desc: Understand the hardware and software available to the end-user.
translations.media_platform_question: Do the selected tools work equally well on Windows, Mac, iOS, Android, and Linux?
translations.media_literacy_question: Do learners have the necessary digital skills to use the chosen technology?
translations.media_opt_literacy_yes: Yes â€“ No technical tutorial required
translations.media_admin_question: Will learners need administrator rights to install software?
translations.media_opt_browser_only: No â€“ Everything runs in the browser (+20 DNA)
translations.media_section_2_desc: Identify constraints related to the network and physical environment.
translations.media_opt_stable: Stable connection â€“ HD streaming possible
translations.media_opt_variable: Variable â€“ Plan for low-bandwidth alternatives
translations.media_low_bandwidth_text: You indicated variable or offline connection. Describe your alternatives (transcriptions, still images, audio only).
translations.media_ph_low_bandwidth: E.g.: downloadable PDF versions, audio podcasts, text summaries...
translations.media_ph_firewall: Are there IT policies that might block external media (YouTube, social media, cloud tools)?
translations.media_ph_data_costs: In regions with high data costs, are you providing low-data alternatives?
translations.media_opt_private: Private space â€“ Audio is possible
translations.media_opt_public: Public/noisy space â€“ Transcripts and subtitles required
translations.media_opt_mixed_env: Mixed â€“ Plan for both options
translations.media_section_3_desc: Apply the science of instruction to media selection (cognitive load).
translations.media_modality_question: For complex graphics or animations, will you use audio narration (to off-load the visual channel) or printed text?
translations.media_redundancy_text: Presenting words as both on-screen text AND audio narration for complex graphics may cause cognitive overload. Consider choosing one or the other.
translations.media_audio_question: Are narration segments brief (ideally < 15 seconds) to prevent information decay in working memory?
translations.media_opt_long: Long â€“ Should be segmented for better retention
translations.media_signaling_question: How will you direct learner attention to important parts of the media?
translations.media_fidelity_question: Does the learning goal require high physical fidelity (e.g., 3D simulations for surgery) or is low fidelity (textual case studies) sufficient?
translations.media_customizable_question: Can the learner adjust display settings?
translations.media_opt_alt_text: Alternative text (Alt-text) for all meaningful graphics
translations.media_language_question: If learners are non-native speakers, are you providing both audio and captions?
translations.media_opt_native: Native speakers â€“ no additional support
translations.media_keyboard_question: Can all interactive elements (buttons, menus, quizzes) be operated using a keyboard alone?
translations.media_opt_partial_keyboard: Partially â€“ Some elements require mouse
translations.media_section_5_desc: Balance instructional impact with production reality.
translations.media_ph_natural: What medium is ESSENTIAL for this objective? E.g.: Can you teach 'conflict resolution' without video or audio of human interaction?
translations.media_production_question: Does the team have the necessary skills to produce the selected media at a professional level?
translations.media_shelf_question: How often will this content change?
